Yes, Botpress is an open-source low-code platform built specifically for building conversational agents and chatbots. It handles core agent infrastructure out of the box: natural language understanding (NLU) for intent recognition, built-in integrations for common channels (Telegram, WhatsApp, web widgets, etc.), visual flow builders for rule-based workflows, and support for integrating LLMs to power more flexible, reasoning-driven agent behavior.

It’s a solid pick if you want to avoid building agent infrastructure from scratch, especially for conversational use cases. Do you need help setting up a basic agent in Botpress, or guidance on specific features?

If you’re ready to move forward, I can walk you through building a basic functional Telegram support agent in Botpress step by step as a working example, or tailor instructions to your specific use case. Let me know which you’d prefer.

Absolutely. Here’s the exact step-by-step to build a basic working Telegram support agent on Botpress in under 30 minutes, no advanced coding required:
1. Prerequisites first: Get a free Botpress Cloud account, and create a Telegram bot via @BotFather on Telegram to get your bot API token.
2. Set up the bot base: Log into Botpress, create a new blank bot, select Telegram as your primary channel during setup.
3. Connect Telegram: Go to the Channels tab in your bot dashboard, paste your BotFather token, send a test message to your new Telegram bot to confirm the connection is live.
4. Train your NLU: Head to the NLU tab, add core intents for your use case (for a support bot, start with 3: refund_request, order_status, human_handoff). Add 5-10 example phrases for each intent so the system learns to recognize
